{"en": {"title": "Grottaglie blue and red ceramic vase", "description": "This blue and red Grottaglie ceramic vase is handmade by Gianluca Annicchiarico, ceramic craftsman from Grottaglie, in the province of Taranto, Puglia. The piece is worked on a wheel and finished with a shiny enamel that combines a deep blue with a very intense red stripe.

The contrast between both colors gives the piece a very graphic and contemporary aesthetic, while maintaining the irregular and unique character of artisanal ceramics. Small variations in glaze, shape and surface are a natural part of the making process and make each piece different.

With approximate measurements of Ø 19 × H 17 cm, it can be used as a decorative container, vase or protagonist piece on a table, shelf or sideboard.

A piece made in Italy that reflects Grottaglie's ceramic tradition from a modern perspective, with color, simplicity and a strong visual presence."}}

{"en": {"title": "Turquoise Blue and Cobalt Ceramic Jar", "description": "This handmade ceramic jar with lid is made and glazed by hand in Puglia, southern Italy, reinterpreting the ceramic tradition of the region from a simple, modern and colorful aesthetic.

Its cylindrical and compact shape makes it a versatile piece for everyday use. The two-tone finish combines a luminous turquoise blue at the bottom with an intense cobalt blue at the top, creating a clean and very Mediterranean contrast.

Small variations in shape, glaze and color intensity are a consequence of the artisanal process and are part of the unique character of each piece.

It can be used as a storage jar, container for small objects or decorative piece, adding color and personality to the kitchen, table, shelf or any corner of the house.

A functional and decorative piece that connects the pottery tradition of Puglia with a contemporary aesthetic."}}

{"en": {"title": "Blue and emerald green jar", "description": "This handmade ceramic jar with lid is made and glazed by hand in Puglia, southern Italy, a region deeply linked to the Mediterranean pottery tradition.

Its simple, slightly truncated silhouette is completed with a matching ceramic lid. The glaze combines an intense emerald green in the upper part with turquoise blue in the lower part, creating an irregular color transition full of nuances that highlights the artisanal nature of the piece.

Manual work means that each jar presents small variations in shape, glaze and color intensity. These differences are part of its uniqueness and make each piece a unique object.

Its design is based on the traditional ceramic containers used in Puglia to store and preserve food, reinterpreted here from a more contemporary aesthetic. It can be used as a storage jar, container for small objects or simply as a decorative element in a kitchen, a shelf or on a table.

A piece with a strong Mediterranean character that combines tradition, color and Italian craftsmanship with a simple and modern design."}}

{"en": {"title": "Blue and violet oil bottle", "description": "This handmade ceramic oil pot is made and painted by hand.

Made in Grottaglie, Puglia, one of the Italian towns most recognized for its ceramic tradition, it combines manual clay work with enamelled decoration made by artisans who have transmitted these techniques from generation to generation.

Its finish in intense blue and violet, with a shiny surface and slight chromatic variations, highlights its rounded shape and gives the piece a very special character. Each oil bottle presents small differences inherent to the artisanal process, so each piece is unique.

It is made with certified enamels suitable for food use, so it can be used as an oil can on the table or in the kitchen. At the same time, its design and color combination allow it to be used as a decorative object, providing a handmade and Mediterranean touch to any space.

A functional and decorative piece that brings together Grottaglie's ceramic tradition with a contemporary and colorful aesthetic."}}

{"en": {"title": "Italian yellow and blue jug", "description": "The handmade ceramic jug is made by hand in Grottaglie.

The enamel finish combines an intense cobalt blue on the top with luminous yellow on the base, united by a subtle green stripe created by the transition between both enamels. A vibrant and Mediterranean combination that turns each jug into a particularly decorative piece. In the central part it has a delicate relief border made on the ceramic itself, providing texture and reinforcing its artisanal character.

Thanks to its manual production, small variations in color, glaze or shape may appear. These irregularities are typical of the artisanal process and make each piece unique and unrepeatable.

Perfect both for serving water or other drinks and for using it as a vase or decorative element, adding color and personality to the table, kitchen or any corner of the house."}}

{"en": {"title": "Italian red and gray jug", "description": "Salento, located in the Puglia region, in southern Italy, has a long pottery tradition that is reflected in the simple and functional forms of this “Brocca”

Its enameled finish combines a deep red on the top with a stone gray tone on the base, creating a contemporary contrast that updates a piece with deeply traditional roots.

Made with natural enamels, each jug presents small variations typical of the artisan work that make each piece a unique object.

Artisan production Made in Salento, for Cue Cerámica."}}

{"en": {"title": "Yellow and Green Cape", "description": "The ceramic Capasa recovers one of the traditional forms of domestic ceramics from Puglia. In the past, these pieces were used to preserve food, especially products prepared in oil or vinegar, such as artichokes, eggplants or peppers.

Handcrafted in Grottaglie, this capasa maintains its characteristic cylindrical shape and its two small side handles, reinterpreting an everyday piece as a decorative and functional object for the home and the table. It can also be used as a vase for flowers, branches or decorative compositions, providing a handmade and Mediterranean touch to any space.

Its enamelled finish combines intense yellow on the top and deep green on the base, creating a simple and very characteristic color contrast. The slight variations in the enamel, typical of artisanal production, make each piece unique.

A piece full of personality that unites the ceramic tradition of Grottaglie, Puglia, with a fresh and contemporary aesthetic, perfect for adding color to a table, a kitchen, a shelf or any corner of the house."}}

{"en": {"title": "Traiguera Pitcher", "description": "The Traiguera pitcher is an emblematic piece of traditional pottery from this town located in the extreme north of the Valencian Community, near the border with Tarragona. Traiguera is known for its rich pottery tradition, and its jugs retain deep historical and cultural value.

The Traiguera jugs, also known as "cantes", are characterized by their robust and distinctive shape. These vessels have a bulging, ribbed body, with a narrow base that widens toward the center, forming a prominent belly. The neck of the jug is elongated, and two handles emerge from it that extend downward, resting on the bulging body of the piece.

The decoration of these jugs is done with manganese oxide, applying strokes and stripes distributed over the entire surface. This decoration is carried out using a comb with four, five or six prongs, which gives it a unique and handmade appearance. The clay used to make it is red, finely sifted, and after cooking, it acquires a characteristic straw hue.

These jugs represent not only the technical skill of the Traiguera potters, but also the preservation of a centuries-old tradition that is still alive in the region.
